```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->

Taxonomic classification of the most complete bins with GTDB-Tk. Commands for this step were run in `gtdbtk/`.

```{bash}
#change directory
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
```

```{bash}
#will iterate over our list of topbins. For each of the topbins we want to copy a file corresponding to that bin into our genomes folder.
while read bin;do echo $bin;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

#  to turn this bin name into a path specifying the fasta file for the bin. So for every bin we need to prepend the path to its folder ../metabat/bins_bbd/ and then append the file extension .fa
while read bin;do echo "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa";done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

#perform the copy
while read bin;do cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# check that it worked
ls genomes
```


```{bash}
#created new shell script
#run the job
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh

#check that it produced a summary of its classifications
ls -l out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv

#Now copy the summary up into the gtdbtk folder. Git ignores everything inside out, but it can see a .tsv file saved directly in gtdbtk, so this lets you add the summary to your repository.
cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```
